question:
For decades, Indian farmers were nudged away from millets towards rice and wheat, grains that the public distribution system made cheaper and that the Green Revolution made more abundant. Millets, once the staple of the rural poor, came to be (A)____ to the margins of the national diet, dismissed as 'coarse cereals', a label that carried the faint stigma of poverty. Within a generation, many households that had grown up on ragi, jowar and bajra no longer knew how to cook them. The neglect proved costly. Rice and wheat demand heavy irrigation, and their cultivation has drawn down groundwater in several states at a pace that is (B)____ unsustainable.

Millets, by contrast, thrive on scanty rainfall and poor soil, and several varieties mature in barely ninety days. Nutritionists add that they are rich in fibre, iron and calcium, qualities that make them a valuable addition (C)____ the diet of children and pregnant women. Not only (D)____ they withstand drought, but they also tolerate the erratic temperatures that climate change is bringing. It is hardly surprising, then, that a number of state governments (E)____ now promoting millets through school meals and procurement schemes.

Whether this revival will endure depends on whether consumers, too, can be persuaded to rediscover grains that their grandparents ate without a second thought. Chefs and food companies have begun to help, by presenting millets in forms that urban households find familiar, such as noodles, biscuits and breakfast flakes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (A).
explanation:
नियम: Vocabulary (संदर्भ से अर्थ): Relegate X to Y = X को निचले दर्जे या हाशिये पर धकेल देना (demote, push aside)। 'Come to be + V3' = ऐसा माना / बना दिया जाने लगना। 'to the margins' के साथ अनदेखी का भाव चाहिए, और आगे 'dismissed as coarse cereals' इसी की पुष्टि करता है।

यहाँ: Millets को राष्ट्रीय आहार के हाशिये पर धकेल दिया गया → 'came to be relegated to the margins of the national diet'।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: regulated = नियमों से नियंत्रित किया गया (regulate prices); reiterated = दोहराया गया (reiterate a demand); rejuvenated = फिर से तरोताज़ा / जवान किया गया (rejuvenate the skin)। इनमें से कोई भी 'हाशिये पर धकेलने' का भाव नहीं देता, और 'to the margins' के साथ बेमेल है।

explanation:

यहाँ: Subject 'they' बहुवचन है और आगे 'tolerate', 'is bringing' वर्तमान काल में हैं → 'Not only do they withstand drought'।

question:
Coral reefs occupy less than one per cent of the ocean floor, yet they shelter roughly a quarter of all marine species. This extraordinary density of life has earned them the title of 'rainforests of the sea'. Corals live in a delicate partnership with microscopic algae that give them both colour and nourishment. When the water grows too warm, the corals expel these algae, a process known as bleaching. A bleached reef is not yet dead, but it is starved, and repeated episodes of heat can kill it outright. Over the past three decades, mass bleaching events (A)____ far more frequent, and scientists attribute the trend to the (B)____ warming of the oceans.

The consequences extend well beyond the reefs themselves. Coastal communities depend on them for fish, for tourism and for protection from storms, and the loss of a reef can therefore (C)____ an entire local economy into crisis. Conservation efforts include cutting emissions, restricting destructive fishing and (D)____ damaged reefs by transplanting healthy coral fragments. These measures help, but experts caution that no amount of local effort can compensate for a warming sea. Heat is not the only enemy, for run-off from farms and cities, together with the gradual acidification of seawater, weakens corals still further.

Unless emissions fall sharply, most of the world's reefs (E)____ by the end of the century. It is a prospect that should concern even those who will never visit a reef, for the fish, the shoreline and the livelihoods that depend on it will vanish with it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (A).
explanation:
नियम: Present Perfect (have / has + V3): अतीत में शुरू होकर वर्तमान तक चलने वाली या वर्तमान से जुड़ी क्रिया; संकेत-शब्द — over the past ..., for, since, so far, in recent years, lately। इनके साथ Simple Past नहीं आता।

यहाँ: 'Over the past three decades' से बीते तीस वर्षों से अब तक का संबंध है → 'mass bleaching events have become far more frequent'।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: had become = Past Perfect (किसी बीते समय से पहले पूरी हुई क्रिया); became = Simple Past (निश्चित बीता समय, यहाँ अवधि वर्तमान तक है); are becoming = Present Continuous (अभी हो रही क्रिया, 'over the past three decades' के लिए perfect काल चाहिए)।

यहाँ: 'the loss of a reef can plunge an entire local economy into crisis' = एक रीफ़ का नुकसान पूरी स्थानीय अर्थव्यवस्था को संकट में धकेल सकता है।

यहाँ: 'cutting emissions, restricting destructive fishing and restoring damaged reefs' — तीनों gerunds (V-ing)।

नियम: First Conditional / Unless: Unless (= if not) के clause में Simple Present आता है और मुख्य clause में भविष्य का रूप (will + V1)। 'By the end of the century' जैसे भविष्य के समय-बिंदु के साथ पूरी हो चुकी स्थिति के लिए Future Perfect (will have + V3) आता है।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: would vanish = Unless + Simple Present के साथ 'would' नहीं आता (वह काल्पनिक Second Conditional में आता है); vanished = Simple Past (भविष्य की चेतावनी में बेमेल); had vanished = Past Perfect (किसी बीती घटना से पहले की क्रिया)।

question:
Few inventions have altered the course of history as profoundly as the printing press. Before Johannes Gutenberg perfected movable type in the fifteenth century, books were copied by hand, and a single volume could take a scribe months to complete. Knowledge was, as a result, the preserve of monasteries, universities and the wealthy. No sooner had the new presses begun to operate (A)____ they sprang up in cities across Europe, turning out Bibles, almanacs and pamphlets at a fraction of the earlier cost. A town that had once possessed a handful of manuscripts now found itself flooded with printed sheets of every kind, from sermons and ballads to maps and price lists.

Cheap books (B)____ the way for the Reformation and, later, for the scientific revolution, since ideas could now travel faster than the authorities could suppress them. The press also fostered the growth of vernacular languages, for printers, anxious to sell to the widest possible audience, (C)____ for local tongues rather than Latin. Neither the king nor his ministers (D)____ able to halt the spread of pamphlets that questioned their authority, though many tried by licensing printers and burning books.

It is (E)____ noting, however, that literacy rose slowly; for generations, most people encountered print only when it was read aloud to them. The revolution, in other words, was one of availability before it became one of habit. Libraries, schools and eventually public education had to follow before the printed word could reach the many rather than the few.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (A).
explanation:
नियम: Correlatives: No sooner + had + subject + V3 ... than + subject + V2। जोड़ीदार हमेशा 'than' रहता है; 'Hardly / Scarcely / Barely ... when / before' में 'when' आता है। 'No sooner ... when' ✗।

यहाँ: 'No sooner had the new presses begun to operate than they sprang up in cities across Europe' = मशीनें चालू होते ही वे यूरोप के शहरों में उग आईं।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: when = Hardly / Scarcely का जोड़ीदार; then = तब (समय बताता है, तुलना या जोड़ीदार नहीं); that = कि (No sooner के साथ नहीं आता)।

नियम: Idiom: Pave the way for = किसी चीज़ का रास्ता तैयार करना (to make something possible)। इसी अर्थ के अन्य idioms — lay the foundation / groundwork for, set the stage for, open the door to। 'build / lay / cut the way for' idiom नहीं हैं।

यहाँ: 'Cheap books paved the way for the Reformation' = सस्ती किताबों ने सुधार आंदोलन की राह तैयार की।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: built = बनाया (built a house / a career); laid = बिछाया या रखा (laid the foundation); cut = काटा (cut a path)। 'the way for' के साथ यह idiom इन तीनों से नहीं बनता।

question:
Few inventions have altered the course of history as profoundly as the printing press. Before Johannes Gutenberg perfected movable type in the fifteenth century, books were copied by hand, and a single volume could take a scribe months to complete. Knowledge was, as a result, the preserve of monasteries, universities and the wealthy. No sooner had the new presses begun to operate (A)____ they sprang up in cities across Europe, turning out Bibles, almanacs and pamphlets at a fraction of the earlier cost. A town that had once possessed a handful of manuscripts now found itself flooded with printed sheets of every kind, from sermons and ballads to maps and price lists.

Cheap books (B)____ the way for the Reformation and, later, for the scientific revolution, since ideas could now travel faster than the authorities could suppress them. The press also fostered the growth of vernacular languages, for printers, anxious to sell to the widest possible audience, (C)____ for local tongues rather than Latin. Neither the king nor his ministers (D)____ able to halt the spread of pamphlets that questioned their authority, though many tried by licensing printers and burning books.

It is (E)____ noting, however, that literacy rose slowly; for generations, most people encountered print only when it was read aloud to them. The revolution, in other words, was one of availability before it became one of habit. Libraries, schools and eventually public education had to follow before the printed word could reach the many rather than the few.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (C).
explanation:
नियम: Opt for = चुनना, पसंद करना (choose)। Opt for / opt out of / opt in। वहीं oppose (विरोध करना, सीधा object लेता है), opine (राय देना, 'that' clause के साथ), operate (चलना या चलाना, on / in / through के साथ)।

यहाँ: 'printers ... opted for local tongues rather than Latin' = छापाख़ानों ने लैटिन की जगह स्थानीय भाषाएँ चुनीं।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: opposed = विरोध किया ('opposed for' नहीं बनता); opined = राय व्यक्त की (opined that ...); operated = चलाया / शल्य-क्रिया की। 'for local tongues' के साथ इनका अर्थ नहीं बनता।

explanation:
नियम: Worth + gerund (V-ing): worth + V-ing = करने योग्य (worth reading, worth visiting, worth noting)। 'Worthy' के बाद 'of' आता है (worthy of note); 'valuable' के बाद 'to + V1' (valuable to note)।

question:
Space is no longer the empty void it once seemed. Since the launch of Sputnik in 1957, human beings have filled the orbits around the Earth with thousands of satellites, spent rocket stages and fragments of broken equipment. For years, space agencies (A)____ about the growing risk of collisions, but the warnings have gone largely unheeded. A fleck of paint travelling at orbital speed can punch a hole through a spacecraft window, and a single collision between two large objects can generate thousands of new fragments, each a potential projectile. Even a handful of such events would be enough to make the most useful orbits dangerous for decades.

The danger is compounded by the fact that debris, once created, is almost impossible to remove. A defunct satellite may circle the Earth for decades or even centuries before atmospheric drag (B)____ it down. Some engineers fear a chain reaction, in which each collision (C)____ more debris, which in turn causes more collisions, until certain orbits become unusable. Satellites now provide navigation, weather forecasts and communication, and it is these services, (D)____ the world has come to depend so heavily, that make the problem urgent.

Several proposals for clearing orbits are under study, from nets and harpoons to lasers, but none has yet been tested at scale. Prevention is cheaper than cure, and operators are being urged to retire their satellites promptly, (E)____ they become hazards for others.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (A).
explanation:
नियम: Present Perfect Continuous (have / has been + V-ing): अतीत में शुरू होकर वर्तमान तक लगातार जारी क्रिया, खासकर for / since के साथ। आगे 'the warnings have gone unheeded' वर्तमान तक का संबंध पक्का करता है।

यहाँ: 'For years, space agencies have been warning about the growing risk of collisions' = वर्षों से एजेंसियाँ चेतावनी देती आ रही हैं।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: are warned = Present Passive (एजेंसियाँ चेतावनी पाती हैं, अर्थ उलट जाता); had warned = Past Perfect (किसी बीते समय से पहले की क्रिया, यहाँ वर्तमान तक का संबंध चाहिए); will warn = भविष्य (For years के साथ बेमेल)।

explanation:
नियम: Time clause (before / after / when / until) में सामान्य या भावी कथन के लिए Simple Present आता है, और verb subject के अनुसार लगता है। यहाँ मुख्य clause में 'may circle' है, इसलिए 'before' के बाद भी वर्तमान रूप चाहिए।

यहाँ: Subject 'atmospheric drag' एकवचन है → 'before atmospheric drag brings it down' (हवा के घर्षण के उसे नीचे खींच लाने से पहले)।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: bring = बहुवचन रूप (subject एकवचन है); brought = भूतकाल (may circle के साथ सामान्य कथन में मेल नहीं); bringing = V-ing (finite verb नहीं, clause अधूरा रहता)।

explanation:

यहाँ: 'each collision spawns more debris, which in turn causes more collisions' = हर टक्कर और मलबा पैदा करती है।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: spurns = ठुकराता है, अस्वीकार करता है (spurns an offer); spares = बख़्श देता है, बचा लेता है (spares the rod); spans = फैलता है या पार करता है (a bridge spans a river)। तीनों संदर्भ में बेमेल।

explanation:
नियम: Preposition + relative pronoun: जब verb के साथ fixed preposition हो (depend on) और clause 'which' से शुरू हो, तो preposition पहले आ सकता है — services, on which the world depends। निर्जीव के लिए 'which', व्यक्ति के लिए 'whom'; commas वाले (non-defining) clause में 'that' नहीं आता।

यहाँ: 'these services, on which the world has come to depend so heavily' = ये सेवाएँ, जिन पर दुनिया बहुत अधिक निर्भर हो गई है।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: which = अकेले 'depend which' नहीं बनता (preposition 'on' छूट जाता है); whom = व्यक्तियों के लिए (services निर्जीव हैं); that = comma वाले clause में नहीं आता और preposition भी लुप्त।

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (E).
explanation:
नियम: Lest = ताकि ... न हो (for fear that / so that ... not); इसके बाद 'subject + (should) + V1' आता है और अपने आप में निषेध का भाव है, इसलिए 'not' नहीं लगता — Work hard lest you fail; lest he should forget।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: unless = जब तक ... न (शर्त, यहाँ अर्थ बेमेल); although = यद्यपि (विरोध का भाव); whereas = जबकि (तुलना / विरोध)। इनमें से कोई 'ऐसा न हो कि' का अर्थ नहीं देता।

question:
The gig economy, in which people earn a living through short-term tasks arranged on digital platforms, is often celebrated as a triumph of flexibility. Drivers, delivery riders and freelance designers are told that they are free to work when they please, as if they (A)____ their own bosses. For many, particularly students and those who need a second income, the arrangement is a genuine convenience. The platforms, for their part, insist that they merely connect customers with independent providers and cannot be held answerable for the vagaries of the market. Yet beneath the language of freedom lies a more troubling reality.

Because platforms classify workers as 'partners' rather than employees, they are (B)____ of the obligation to provide a minimum wage, paid leave or insurance. Earnings fluctuate with demand, and a rider who falls ill has no employer to fall back on. Algorithms that allocate work and rate performance can, moreover, (C)____ a worker's income overnight on the strength of a few poor ratings, with no human being to whom the decision can be appealed. Defenders of the model argue that if workers (D)____ these terms they would simply leave. This ignores the fact that many have few alternatives, and that the real choice is often between a poor job and none at all.

Several countries have begun to (E)____ down on the platforms, requiring them to contribute to social security funds for those who work through them. Such measures, if carefully designed, may preserve flexibility while restoring a measure of dignity and security to those who deliver our meals and drive our cars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (A).
explanation:
नियम: As if / As though + were: जब तुलना काल्पनिक या वास्तविकता के उलट हो तो 'as if / as though' के बाद सभी subjects के साथ 'were' आता है — He talks as if he were the owner (जबकि वह मालिक नहीं है)। वास्तविक स्थिति हो तो सामान्य रूप आता है।

यहाँ: प्लेटफ़ॉर्म कहते हैं कि वे अपने मालिक खुद हैं, जबकि वास्तव में ऐसा नहीं है → 'as if they were their own bosses'।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: are = वास्तविक तथ्य बताता (यहाँ भाव काल्पनिक है); will be = भविष्य; had been = अतीत की काल्पनिक स्थिति (as if ... had been, पिछली घटना के लिए)।

Algorithms that allocate work and rate performance can, moreover, (C)____ a worker's income overnight on the strength of a few poor ratings, with no human being to whom the decision can be appealed. Defenders of the model argue that if workers (D)____ these terms they would simply leave. This ignores the fact that many have few alternatives, and that the real choice is often between a poor job and none at all.

Several countries have begun to (E)____ down on the platforms, requiring them to contribute to social security funds for those who work through them. Such measures, if carefully designed, may preserve flexibility while restoring a measure of dignity and security to those who deliver our meals and drive our cars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (D).
explanation:
नियम: Second Conditional (काल्पनिक वर्तमान या भविष्य): If + subject + V2, subject + would / could / might + V1। If-clause में 'would' नहीं लगता।

यहाँ: main clause में 'would simply leave' है, इसलिए if-clause में Past Simple चाहिए → 'if workers disliked these terms, they would simply leave'।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: dislike = Simple Present (तब main clause में 'will leave' आता); would dislike = if-clause में 'would' नहीं लगता; had disliked = Third Conditional (तब main clause में 'would have left' चाहिए)।

The gig economy, in which people earn a living through short-term tasks arranged on digital platforms, is often celebrated as a triumph of flexibility. Drivers, delivery riders and freelance designers are told that they are free to work when they please, as if they (A)____ their own bosses. For many, particularly students and those who need a second income, the arrangement is a genuine convenience. The platforms, for their part, insist that they merely connect customers with independent providers and cannot be held answerable for the vagaries of the market. Yet beneath the language of freedom lies a more troubling reality.

Because platforms classify workers as 'partners' rather than employees, they are (B)____ of the obligation to provide a minimum wage, paid leave or insurance. Earnings fluctuate with demand, and a rider who falls ill has no employer to fall back on. Algorithms that allocate work and rate performance can, moreover, (C)____ a worker's income overnight on the strength of a few poor ratings, with no human being to whom the decision can be appealed. Defenders of the model argue that if workers (D)____ these terms they would simply leave. This ignores the fact that many have few alternatives, and that the real choice is often between a poor job and none at all.

Several countries have begun to (E)____ down on the platforms, requiring them to contribute to social security funds for those who work through them. Such measures, if carefully designed, may preserve flexibility while restoring a measure of dignity and security to those who deliver our meals and drive our cars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (E).
explanation:
नियम: Phrasal verb: Crack down on = किसी पर सख़्त कार्रवाई करना (take strict action against)। अन्य: break down (ख़राब होना / टूटना), bring down (गिराना), turn down (ठुकराना या आवाज़ घटाना)।

यहाँ: कई देश प्लेटफ़ॉर्म पर सख़्ती कर रहे हैं और उन्हें सामाजिक सुरक्षा कोष में योगदान देने को कह रहे हैं → 'begun to crack down on the platforms'।

विकल्पों के अर्थ: break down on / bring down on / turn down on इस अर्थ में प्रयोग नहीं होते; break down = ख़राब होना, bring down = गिरा देना, turn down = प्रस्ताव ठुकराना। कार्रवाई करने का भाव सिर्फ़ 'crack down on' में है।
